statement:
(i) Show that $\cos 15^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}$ and find a similar expression for $\sin 15^\circ$.

(ii) Show that $\cos\alpha$ is a root of the equation
$$4x^3-3x-\cos 3\alpha=0,$$
and find the other two roots in terms of $\cos\alpha$ and $\sin\alpha$.

(iii) Use parts (i) and (ii) to solve the equation $y^3-3y-\sqrt2=0$, giving your answers in surd form.
solution:
(i) Using the compound angle formula $\cos 15^\circ=\cos(45^\circ-30^\circ)$:
$$\cos15^\circ=\cos45^\circ\cos30^\circ+\sin45^\circ\sin30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}+\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}.$$

Similarly,
$$\sin15^\circ=\sin45^\circ\cos30^\circ-\cos45^\circ\sin30^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac{\sqrt3}{2}-\frac{\sqrt2}{2}\cdot\frac12=\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}=\frac{\sqrt3-1}{2\sqrt2}.$$

(ii) The triple-angle formula is $\cos3\alpha=4\cos^3\alpha-3\cos\alpha$. Rearranging,
$$4\cos^3\alpha-3\cos\alpha-\cos3\alpha=0,$$
so $x=\cos\alpha$ is a root of $4x^3-3x-\cos3\alpha=0$.

The other two roots are $\cos(\alpha+120^\circ)$ and $\cos(\alpha-120^\circ)$. Using compound-angle formulae,
$$\cos(\alpha\pm120^\circ)=\cos\alpha\cos120^\circ\mp\sin\alpha\sin120^\circ=-\tfrac12\cos\alpha\mp\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\alpha.$$

So the three roots are
$$\cos\alpha,\qquad -\tfrac12\cos\alpha-\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\alpha,\qquad -\tfrac12\cos\alpha+\tfrac{\sqrt3}{2}\sin\alpha.$$

(iii) Compare $y^3-3y-\sqrt2=0$ with $4x^3-3x-\cos3\alpha=0$. Substituting $y=2x$:
$$y^3-3y=(2x)^3-3(2x)=8x^3-6x=2(4x^3-3x)=2\cos3\alpha.$$

So $2\cos3\alpha-\sqrt2=0$, giving $\cos3\alpha=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{2}$. Hence $3\alpha=45^\circ,315^\circ,405^\circ,\dots$, so $\alpha=15^\circ,105^\circ,135^\circ$ (or any three values $120^\circ$ apart).

Therefore $y=2\cos\alpha$ takes the three values
$$y=2\cos15^\circ=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2},\qquad y=2\cos105^\circ=\frac{\sqrt2-\sqrt6}{2},\qquad y=2\cos135^\circ=-\sqrt2.$$

(using $\cos15^\circ=\frac{\sqrt3+1}{2\sqrt2}=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{4}$ and $\cos105^\circ=-\cos75^\circ=-\frac{\sqrt6-\sqrt2}{4}$.)

Hence the solutions are
$$y=\frac{\sqrt6+\sqrt2}{2},\qquad \frac{\sqrt2-\sqrt6}{2},\qquad -\sqrt2.$$
